hooks.voice: Every morning my to-do list got longer. And I started nothing.
hooks.visual: Alex at the desk, laptop open, looks at camera (S01).
hooks.payoff: One task and one 25-minute timer replace the choosing; no streak to lose.

hooks.voice: Your to-do list is the reason you don't start.
hooks.visual: Alex points at a long list on a sticky note (S01 alt).
hooks.payoff: A long list makes you choose first, and choosing feels like work.
hooks.risk: Medium: sounds absolute; soften to 'my list'.

hooks.voice: Why is starting harder than the work itself?
hooks.visual: Close-up of the start screen question (task.png).
hooks.payoff: Because a long list asks for a decision before any work.
hooks.risk: Low; question hooks can feel generic.

hooks.voice: This card is how my mornings used to go.
hooks.visual: Notification card slams in over the desk: 'Quick question (5 min?)'.
hooks.payoff: The app asks one question instead: what is the one task?
hooks.risk: Card is illustrative and must stay labeled.

hooks.visual: Phone: task screen → Start → timer running (task.png → timer.png).
hooks.payoff: Shows the one-task start on example UI.
hooks.risk: Medium: product-first opening may read as an ad.

hooks.voice: Twenty-five minutes on one task beat my whole list.
hooks.visual: Done screen with the full ring (done.png).
hooks.payoff: Explains why one task is easier to start than a list.
hooks.risk: High: reads like an outcome promise; avoid.
